title: Phase-Coherent Spin and Lattice Modulations in a Y-type Hexaferrite
authors: Oskar Stepančić, Annika Stellhorn, Emma Campillo, Kun Zhai, Niklas Ekström, A. Corani, D. Alba Venero, R. Cubitt, E. Blackburn, L. Shen
abstract: Spin-driven multiferroics owe their electric polarization to lattice distortions that follow the magnetic order, yet in incommensurate magnets symmetry normally forbids such a distortion at the fundamental magnetic wavevector, and the distortions themselves are rarely observed. Here we use half-polarized neutron scattering to show that the Y-type hexaferrite Ba$_{0.4}$Sr$_{1.6}$Mg$_2$Fe$_{12}$O$_{22}$ hosts, in its saturated high-field state, a magnetic modulation and a longitudinal lattice modulation at one and the same wavevector, locked in phase. The signature is a large nuclear-magnetic interference asymmetry, $r$ ~ 0.8, of the same sign at the two conjugate satellites and persisting to 275 K. The zone contrast and the field dependence of the satellite indicate an internal, field-induced longitudinal distortion. The modulated state coexists with the transverse-conical magnetoelectric phase and outlives it, revealing a fundamental-wavevector spin-lattice coupling in a magnetic field regime previously regarded as a simple ferrimagnet.
summary: This work uses half-polarized neutron scattering on a hexaferrite to investigate spin-lattice coupling in an incommensurate magnet. The researchers demonstrate the existence of a field-induced, phase-coherent longitudinal lattice modulation locked to the magnetic modulation at the fundamental wavevector. This observation challenges conventional symmetry rules and reveals a fundamental magnetoelastic coupling mechanism in the material.
main_problem: The study investigates spin-lattice coupling in incommensurate magnets, specifically addressing the observation of lattice distortions at the fundamental magnetic wavevector where symmetry rules typically forbid them.
main_result: The Y-type hexaferrite hosts a phase-coherent magnetic and longitudinal lattice modulation at the fundamental wavevector in its high-field state, evidenced by a large, persistent nuclear-magnetic interference asymmetry.
method: Half-polarized neutron scattering was employed to measure the nuclear-magnetic interference asymmetry ($r$) at conjugate satellite positions, providing a sensitive probe of coupled magnetic and structural order.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Y-type hexaferrite $	ext{Ba}_{0.4}	ext{Sr}_{1.6}	ext{Mg}_2	ext{Fe}_{12}	ext{O}_{22}$. The analysis focuses on the magnetoelastic coupling mechanism enabled by a uniform magnetic moment ($\mathbf{M}_0$) in the presence of an incommensurate magnetic modulation ($\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{q}}$).
key_observables: The normalized asymmetry $r$, the field dependence of satellite intensities ($	ext{k}_0, 	ext{k}_2, 	ext{k}_3$), and the temperature dependence of the modulation amplitude and phase.
important_parameters: The measurements are performed in the saturated high-field state, with key observations persisting up to 275 K and requiring fields above $\approx 2 	ext{ T}$ to resolve the $	ext{k}_3$ satellite.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the interpretation of the asymmetry parameter $r$ to isolate the nuclear-magnetic interference term, which confirms the coupling between the magnetic modulation and an internal lattice distortion.
figures_summary: Figures detail the field evolution of scattering intensities across different wavevectors ($	ext{k}_0, 	ext{k}_2, 	ext{k}_3$), and show the temperature and field dependence of the $\pm	ext{k}_3$ pair asymmetry parameters, confirming the sign consistency of the interference signal.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical context regarding symmetry constraints on structural response in incommensurate magnets. It then presents neutron scattering data showing the appearance and persistence of the $	ext{k}_3$ satellite. The core of the work uses polarization analysis to confirm that the observed signal is due to a field-enabled, phase-coherent coupling between the magnetic and lattice modulations.
why_interesting: While primarily experimental, the detailed analysis of symmetry-forbidden coupling mechanisms and the use of polarization-sensitive scattering techniques provide rigorous physical constraints on the coupling terms ($\mathbf{M}_0 \mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{q}}$) relevant to emergent order parameters in condensed matter systems.
